voice_notes: Webber is a polite, cheerful little boy sharing one body and one head with a spider: he says 'we/us/our head', slips into 'I/me' when the boy remembers home ('Mum always said...', 'I want my nightlight'), treats scary things as playmates ('We'll dance with you, Mr. Shadow!') and jokes about his own crowded head ('What's one more voice in our head?'). PT-BR carries him with colloquial 'a gente' plus 'tá/pra', 'A mamãe', 'nós dois' for 'us both' and 'Sr. Sombra' (e.g. 'Acho que a gente não devia brincar com isso...', 'É mais fácil para nós dois.'). Simplified Chinese uses 我们 for the shared self, 我俩 for 'the two of us', 妈妈 for Mum and 影子先生 for Mr. Shadow, and reuses 又冰又滑 for nightmare fuel ('难得碰到我俩都喜欢的！'). Russian keeps мы/нам/нас, 'нам обоим', 'Мама говорила...', polite вы toward 'Мистер Тень', and plain е rather than ё ('Проще нам обоим.', 'На один голос в голове больше!').

line_notes.codex: Replaces 'I don't think we should play with that...' with a child obeying Mum's rule to the letter while finding the loophole, which shows he now uses the book.
line_notes.codex_needsfuel: Webber mothers everything (spider babies, kitcoons), so an empty book is simply hungry, and the fuel is described the way he already describes nightmare fuel: 'cold and slippery'.
line_notes.no_max_sanity: Builds on his 'one more voice in our head' joke: his head already holds a boy and a spider, so the failure is about room in his mind, not about the book.
line_notes.shadow_mine: A shadow copy of someone who is already two beings throws his counting off, and 'Hi, us!' echoes his greeting to other Webbers ('A spiderfriend! Hi %s!').
line_notes.shadow_other: He uses his official 'Mr. Shadow' and treats the stray copy like a lost pet or child, politely asking who it belongs to.
